name: Saudi Arabia
summary: Saudi Arabia, Day 207. Three things converged in five days. First, the pipeline: Bloomberg's 16-Sep 'half capacity within days' has produced no barrel — Yanbu has loaded nothing since 11 Sep and Kpler's independent estimate is half of exports 'within a month'. The kingdom's answer has been to push crude the other way, THROUGH Hormuz under US escort at 2.8–2.9 mb/d (four times August), loading seven VLCCs at once at Ras Tanura on 20 Sep and transferring ship-to-ship off Sohar — and to tell every European term buyer that October allocations are zero, the first direct Saudi supply cut to Europe of the cycle. Second, the war reached the capital: a Houthi ballistic missile at Riyadh was intercepted at dawn on 19 Sep while Reuters imagery and the WSJ showed a fire at King Khalid airport's fuel farm; two days earlier drone debris in Taif produced the first Saudi civilian death since the 2022 truce. Third, the ally declined: after MBS's 17-Sep call Trump ordered the Pentagon to prepare strikes on the Houthis, then cancelled them on 20 Sep with bombs loading, because the Houthis had promised Oman's channel they would spare everyone but Saudi hulls and his advisers did not want a new front. What Riyadh got instead was a $24.3bn F-35 approval, British refuelling tankers, Turkish and Pakistani pledges under a Mecca Pact nobody has activated, and a seat at today's Trump–GCC meeting. The graph's RESTART trigger stays watching; the new watch is whether Riyadh escalates alone against Sanaa or invokes the pact within 14 days.

recent_signals.headline: **WASHINGTON ORDERED, THEN CANCELLED, A US AIR CAMPAIGN AGAINST THE HOUTHIS AT MBS'S REQUEST — the Saudi ask into today's Trump–GCC meeting is unanswered.** NYT (multi-official, 20–21 Sep): Wed 16 Sep Trump told advisers he opposed strikes; Thu 17 Sep after a call with MBS he reversed and ordered the Pentagon to prepare; midday Sun 20 Sep — target lists approved, munitions being loaded, first wave imminent — he cancelled. Reasons per NYT: the Houthis, via Oman, had assured Washington they would not attack US forces or non-Saudi shipping and an official warned strikes 'would likely collapse' that understanding; Trump's inner circle 'deeply skeptical of or directly opposed'; strain on forces engaged with Iran; doubts that limited strikes would force Houthi talks. Axios ran its own sourced account; Reuters partly confirmed; CENTCOM referred to the White House, which declined on-record comment. Trump (Fox, Sun): 'The Houthis… have so far agreed not to attack American forces… they don't want to fight us.' Framing caution: Euronews/JPost headlines say cancelled 'after Saudi plea/MBS call' — the NYT sequence has MBS's call TRIGGERING preparation; 'Saudi plea caused the stand-down' is unsupported. No Saudi public reaction found. — REPORTED (strong: NYT + Axios + partial Reuters + Trump on record).

**RIYADH STRUCK BY THE HOUTHIS FOR THE FIRST TIME THIS WAR (first Riyadh alert since the July escalation) — a Houthi ballistic missile intercepted at dawn Sat 19 Sep; black smoke from King Khalid International Airport's fuel-storage area.** Coalition (Maj-Gen al-Maliki, SPA): missile toward Riyadh 'intercepted and destroyed'; attempts on Bisha/Baish, Taif, Farasan and YANBU 'thwarted'; no casualties or damage. Houthi Saree: two operations — 'sensitive targets' in Riyadh (ballistic/cruise/drones) and Aramco facilities at Yanbu. Independent: two air-raid alerts over Riyadh (lifted); residents heard explosions; **Reuters imagery showed 'a large plume of black smoke' from the fuel-storage area near KKIA and the WSJ reported a strike hit a jet-fuel facility there, with flight disruptions** (Fox live citing WSJ); Civil Defence 'danger' alert then all-clear. Verdict: an attack reached the capital's airport perimeter — CONFIRMED (missile, interception, fire); whether warhead or interceptor debris caused the fire — REPORTED/unresolved; 'sensitive sites hit' — CLAIMED. Preceded by the first Saudi civilian death since the 2022 truce (Taif, Thu 17 Sep — drone debris killed a Yemeni resident, injured a Saudi and a Pakistani). Reactions: Jordan/UN/GCC condemned; State renewed the ME travel alert; Trump cut short Camp David. UK (PM Burnham, Mon 21 Sep) agreed RAF Voyager tankers for defensive refuelling of Saudi jets for 'several weeks'; State approved a $24.3bn/48 F-35 sale to Saudi Arabia (18 Sep); Turkey's Fidan signalled 'potential military aid'; Pakistan's ISPR chief pledged defence 'to any extent… diplomatically and physically' (18 Sep) — Mecca Pact referenced, NOT activated. (SPA; Al Jazeera 19 Sep; Business Standard/Al Arabiya 20 Sep; Reuters imagery & WSJ via Fox live; AP 21 Sep; Al Jazeera 18 Sep) — CONFIRMED as detailed.

**THE 'DAYS' CLOCK RUNS OUT ~23 SEP WITH NO RESTART: no Aramco/SPA statement and no tracker print of Yanbu loadings 17–21 Sep; Kpler (17 Sep): zero crude loaded at Yanbu since 11 Sep and a partial bypass restores 'only about half of exports within a month' — slower than Bloomberg/Wright's 'half within days'.** The substitute route is the story: satellite/JPM — 2.8–2.9 mb/d THROUGH Hormuz over the six days to ~18–20 Sep (vs ~0.7 in Aug); Aramco loaded ~14mb onto SEVEN VLCCs simultaneously at Ras Tanura Sun 20 Sep ('highest tanker count at Saudi terminals since June'); Bloomberg (via OilPrice 18 Sep): ~60mb sold from Ras Tanura for Sep/Oct loading, ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar, 1–1.5 mb/d redirected to China/Korea/India/Japan. **The cost landed on Europe: Aramco told ALL European term buyers their October allocations are ZERO (Bloomberg, at least two refiners told directly)** — the Yanbu→SUMED→Sidi Kerir path is shut. Kpler counted only five laden Saudi tankers exiting via Bab el-Mandeb in the week; Yanbu storage reported <15mb (oprep 19 Sep). Wright (17 Sep) reframed from 'days' to 'rerouted through Oman'. Note: Kpler attributes the 10-Sep pumping-station strikes to 'Houthi forces'; Riyadh and Baghdad place the launch in Maysan, Iraq (no claimant) — the graph follows the governments. (Kpler blog; Bloomberg 16 & 18 Sep; TE/Mitrade/Fox for satellite/JPM; oprep) — rerouting & zero-Europe CONFIRMED; restart = GUIDANCE, unmet.

**A drone intercepted 'south of Makkah' at 18:50 on 15 Sep — the first Mecca air-defence alert in nearly a decade.** Coalition spokesman al-Maliki attributed it to the Houthis, called it the second attempt on Mecca after a July 2017 missile, and said the two holy mosques are a 'red line'; coalition also confirmed 13 civilians wounded and 7 houses damaged at Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif from Houthi fire. The Houthis CATEGORICALLY DENY targeting Mecca (Saba: 'we categorically deny… any threat… directed at the city of Mecca'; Saree: operations 'far removed from holy places') and CLAIM a Saudi F-15 downed over Marib (no Saudi confirmation, no wreckage). Qatar — the Gulf's mediator — called it 'a shameful act of aggression' and 'a grave escalation.' Saudi strikes on Taiz killed 3 incl. 2 children (Houthi Health Ministry, CLAIMED). Interception = CONFIRMED (Saudi); Houthi origin = CLAIMED vs DENIED; F-15 = CLAIMED. (Al Jazeera/CNBC/Yemen Monitor; Saba via Euronews; ToI for Qatar).

**East-West pipeline: restart GUIDED, not confirmed.** Bloomberg (16 Sep, company sources): Aramco targets ~HALF of the 4–5 mb/d line 'within days' by bypassing the damaged section, full capacity in ~6 weeks; AP: pumping-station repairs 3–5 weeks with 'partial operations possible'; US Energy Sec Wright (CNBC, 15 Sep, from the G20 energy meeting): 'a brief and temporary interruption… measured in days' — a US official guiding Saudi infrastructure; CNBC's caveat: independent analysts read satellite imagery of a pumping station as weeks. FACTS: Yanbu loadings suspended, ZERO Saudi crude departed since 11 Sep (Vortexa); Aramco cancelled some late-Sept European cargoes; Yanbu held 5–7 days of export stock. THE WORKAROUND IS THROUGH HORMUZ: Vortexa shows 22mb loaded on 12 VLCCs at Ras Tanura/Juaymah in the week of 7–13 Sep vs 6–7 vessels in prior weeks, under US escort (Axios: Saudi 'significantly increased' tankers through the strait; daytime escorts begun). Brent −2.7% on the guidance. The RESTART trigger (Aramco/SPA statement OR Kpler-verified Yanbu >2 mb/d) has NOT fired. Retaliation: NO Saudi response to Iraq for a 5th day ('holding off at Baghdad's request'); Cabinet (15 Sep) affirmed the 'legitimate right to defend itself'; MBS received CENTCOM's Adm. Cooper in Jeddah (14 Sep, SPA) and flew to Cairo (15 Sep); Egypt: Saudi security is 'an integral part of Egypt's national security.' Iraq: investigation continues; suspicion on Badr and Harakat Ansar Allah al-Awfiya (FDD, hawkish; JPost concurs). (Bloomberg via Investing.com; CNBC; OilPrice; Vortexa via oprep; SPA/The National) — CONFIRMED (shut, cancellations, re-routing) / REPORTED (restart timeline).

**A full second war with the Houthis, in both directions.** 8 Sep: a Houthi drone/missile wave on Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jizan and Najran wounded 73 civilians, ignited fires at several oil facilities and utilities and halted operations at some energy sites; FT: Aramco's Jazan facilities (400 kb/d refinery) hit; Aramco no comment (AP/NPR/ToI/The National — CONFIRMED). Coalition (al-Malki): 'all necessary operational measures'. Saudi air strikes on Mocha airport and Saada (13 Sep, Houthi media/CBS); Houthis claim a drone/missile strike on Sharurah base (13 Sep, Saree); a projectile wounded two and damaged a mosque in Jazan/al-Tawwal (Saudi civil defence, 13 Sep). The Houthis now hold the entire Yemeni Red Sea coast and Perim — the Yanbu-to-Asia route runs under their guns. Saudi filed amendments to the Iran–Oman lane and (with Bahrain) effectively blocked the Salalah meeting. TASI 10,864.57 (13 Sep).

**THE EAST-WEST PIPELINE — SAUDI'S HORMUZ BYPASS — IS SHUT; THE YANBU TRIGGER FIRED.** UAV attacks on 10 Sep hit pumping stations in the Riyadh and Medina areas (NASA thermal detection 10 Sep; Reuters-verified satellite imagery of a ~60-mile smoke plume and extensive fire damage; several injured); Saudi announced the 'temporary' closure on 11 Sep. Capacity 4–5 mb/d (7 mb/d nameplate) ≈ 4% of global supply — the route that carried Saudi exports around Hormuz since March (Bab el-Mandeb flows rose 5.4 → 8.1 mb/d in Q2 because of it). Yanbu holds 5–7 days of export inventory. Reuters sources (13 Sep): repairs 'partial restoration' to 'five to six weeks' for full. April precedent: a strike cut throughput to 700 kb/d, restored in 3 days — this is worse. Drones originated in Iraq (Maysan); no claim; Trump: Iran 'probably responsible'; Pusztai: 'most likely an order from Tehran'; Iran silent (NOT FOUND). Riyadh reserves 'all measures necessary' but is holding off 'at the Iraqi PM's request'; MBS asked Trump for US strikes on the Houthis — declined (intel/targeting support offered). Brent: $101 (9 Sep) → $107.63 (10 Sep) → $108 (14 Sep). (Saudi statement via AP; Al Jazeera; Bloomberg/CNBC/CNN; Reuters via ToI/Al Arabiya; OilPrice — CONFIRMED)

SAUDI COUNTERSTRIKE FIRED (25 Jul): Saudi coalition forces struck Houthi targets in Yemen after the Houthi tanker attacks, and Saudi air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Yanbu oil refineries. The 24-Jul 'mulling' became confirmed military action — the higher rung (Houthis targeting Saudi PRODUCTION infrastructure, Saudi answering kinetically) is now realized. US+UK also struck the Houthis; US+Saudi struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq (~29 Jul). CONFIRMED (CNBC + Deccan Herald + Gulf News).

recent_signals.headline: NEGATIVE FINDING — no new Iranian strike on Saudi territory in the 17-19 Jul window, and no Arab News or Al Arabiya editorial either. The Saudi-orbit delegitimisation campaign flagged on 17 Jul did NOT continue, consistent with the Soufan Center's read that Riyadh prefers accommodation while Abu Dhabi runs comparatively hawkish — a GCC fissure call that is currently HOLDING and is testable. Saudi Arabia did join the GCC Secretary-General's collective condemnation. Structural note for the bypass arithmetic: the Saudi East-West pipeline to Yanbu has ~3-5 mb/d of spare capacity but exits into the RED SEA, i.e. it carries its own Bab el-Mandeb/Houthi risk and is not a clean Hormuz workaround. CONFIRMED (the absences).

**Saudi Arabia is now fighting a second war it did not choose — and its Hormuz workaround is the target.** The Houthis declared a maritime embargo on the Kingdom on 20 July after the 13 July Houthi ballistic-missile salvo at **Abha airport** — the first Houthi-Saudi exchange in years — and renewed Hodeidah fighting. The Saudi MFA expressed 'the Kingdom's strongest condemnation' of 'the so-called military spokesperson of the terrorist Houthi militia' and said Riyadh 'continues to support the brotherly Yemeni people and their legitimate government.' **MEE reports Saudi Arabia is mulling military escalation in response — the first credible sign of a Gulf state considering kinetic counter-escalation this cycle.** The commercial stakes are exact: with Hormuz shut, Riyadh has been pushing crude across the **East-West Petroline (1,201 km, Abqaiq to Yanbu, ~7m bpd nameplate)** and out through Bab el-Mandeb, where **Yanbu loadings average ~4m bpd against ~973k bpd a year earlier — a more than fourfold increase.** The National reports **Saudi oil loadings down 36% as Houthi threats disrupt Bab al-Mandeb passage.** Riyadh is escalating RHETORICALLY and de-escalating OPERATIONALLY: Arab News editorialises against Iran while the FM works the phones with Bahrain, Egypt and Türkiye, and the Saudi Crown Prince telephoned Aoun to voice support for Lebanon. CONFIRMED.

**Saudi Arabia rejected the Houthi maritime embargo and 'vows to protect shipping' — but has taken no offensive military action.** The embargo turned three Saudi-crude tankers back in the Red Sea (AIS-confirmed) and Saudi loadings are -36% on the threat; the Saudi Crown Prince also telephoned Aoun to voice support for Lebanon. Riyadh is escalating rhetorically and holding operationally — no strikes reported. The commercial stakes are unchanged and precise: the East-West Petroline to Yanbu is the Hormuz workaround the Houthi declaration targets. MEE's 'Saudi mulling military escalation' from the prior window has NOT converted to action. CONFIRMED (rhetoric) / no offensive action.

**Two Saudi tankers struck by the Houthis (Encelia, Layla; one ablaze, crew safe) — and Riyadh has NOT retaliated militarily.** Saudi SPA confirmed the targeting; Saudi 'vows to protect shipping' but the 'mulling military escalation' from the prior window is STILL unconverted to action. Saudi loadings -36% on the threat. THE STRATEGIC COUNTERWEIGHT: the same window, a US-Saudi NUCLEAR COOPERATION PACT was announced ('historic') — Riyadh deepening US ties precisely as its tankers burn, which binds it CLOSER to Washington and further reduces any chance it restricts US operations. The commercial stakes are unchanged: the East-West Petroline to Yanbu is the Hormuz workaround the Houthi strike targets. CONFIRMED (strike, no retaliation) / REPORTED (nuclear pact).
